title: Theban tomb reveals how Egyptian burial trends evolved in time
gist: A study of Theban tomb TT 209 documents how Egyptian burial practices shifted over centuries from individual elaborate-coffin burials to denser reuse and vertical superposition of bodies, with declining coffin use and a shift toward the body's integrity over its container.

insights.claim: Excavation of Theban tomb TT 209's Side Chamber 3 revealed 16 mummified people, a mummified dog, and a chamber of disarticulated remains, showing burial trends shifted from individual coffined interments to reuse and vertical superposition over centuries.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette

insights.claim: Roughly 80 percent of first-millennium-BCE Theban tombs contain remains from different time periods in shared space, indicating systematic tomb reuse rather than chaotic accumulation.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Contextual data point on ancient reuse patterns; scholarly interest only.

insights.claim: Researchers argue each new deposition was adapted to previous bodies in a 'spatial logic' of funerary memory, with declining coffin use reflecting a shift toward the integrity of the body and ritual efficacy over the container itself.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.quote: a kind of funerary memory in the processes of reuse
